newsitem.title: GERMANY: Late German intervention grain offers detailed.
newsitem.headline: Late German intervention grain offers detailed.

text.p: Some 104,566 tonnes of grain were offered into German intervention stores over the last fortnight as the November/May 1996/97 season draws to a close, data from state board BLE showed on Monay.
Volumes offered between May 9 and May 23 included 55,021 tonnes of barley, 31,570 tonnes of rye and 17,830 tonnes of wheat.
Traders said feed grain prices in the free market had fallen fast and this encouraged offers into intervention.
But total grain volumes still lagged those of last year.
By May 23, a total 1,217,246 tonnes had been offered, compared with 1,655,163 tonnes a year earlier.
The offers have been accepted, but have not yet been delivered to stores. Sellers may withdraw offers and BLE may refuse acceptance on quality grounds.
The May buying-in price for all grains is at 248.61 marks/tonne.
